government.note: Parliamentary constitutional monarchy with a ceremonial monarch. Governments are usually minority coalitions relying on support parties in the unicameral Folketing. A constitutional amendment must be passed by two parliaments with an election in between and then approved in a referendum; one third of the Folketing may put most passed bills to a referendum, and EU treaty changes have in practice always been put to a referendum. The Kingdom includes the self-governing Faroe Islands and Greenland, which each elect two members of the Folketing.

offices.note: Heirs are the line of succession on 2000-01-01 under the 1953 Act (male-preference primogeniture): Crown Prince Frederik, Prince Joachim and Joachim's son Nikolai (born 1999). The 2009 referendum introduced absolute primogeniture; Christian became Crown Prince on 14 January 2024.

system.note: 175 members are elected in Denmark proper: 135 constituency seats by D'Hondt in 10 multi-member constituencies plus 40 levelling seats (largest remainder) for parties with at least 2% nationally or a constituency seat. The Faroe Islands and Greenland each elect 2 further members separately. seats_2000 is the March 1998 result adjusted for the four Progress Party members who formed the Freedom 2000 group on 12 October 1999; other individual defections before 1 January 2000 were not checked.
